claims.statement: GatewayService is an unexported Android foreground service (foregroundServiceType dataSync|specialUse) driven by ACTION_START/ACTION_STOP/ACTION_RETRY_NOW intents; ACTION_STOP shuts down the supervisor, stops the foreground notification and stopSelf()s with START_NOT_STICKY, while start/retry return START_STICKY and a null intent (START_STICKY revival after process death) is handled as ACTION_START, which is non-blocking because the supervisor loop performs all work.

The UI-visible running state of the gateway is derived from the supervisor's StateFlow: GatewayService.isServiceRunning is true only for CONNECTED/CONNECTING/RECONNECTING supervisor states, and supervisorStateFlow/supervisorState mirror the supervisor rather than being hand-set booleans that components poke.

On a non-user-initiated death (onDestroy while the runtime isEnabled flag and consent are still set), GatewayService schedules a 15-second AlarmManager watchdog (setExactAndAllowWhileIdle when exact alarms are permitted, inexact setAndAllowWhileIdle fallback otherwise) that revives the service with ACTION_START even from Doze; the redundant revival is harmless because ConnectionSupervisor.start() is idempotent.

The persistent low-importance notification mirrors every ConnectionSupervisor state (waiting for network, reconnecting, retrying, stopped), appends live GMweb outbox-poller bridge telemetry when CONNECTED, and carries a Stop Gateway action that fires ACTION_STOP.

GatewayService.onCreate wires BackendClient, RegistrationManager, HeartbeatManager, OutboxPoller, EventUploader (PR-02) and SecureCommandPoller (PR-10), and the NetworkMonitor singleton, then obtains the ConnectionSupervisor singleton with a newServer factory that constructs GatewayServer(context, prefs.port, prefs.apiKey, bindAllInterfaces = prefs.bindAllInterfaces) and a ManagedComponents adapter that drives heartbeat start/stop/retryNow, outbox poller start/stop, eventUploader start/stop, commandPoller start/stop, and TelephonySyncCoordinator.ensureLoopRunning().

ConnectionSupervisor replaces per-component retry logic with one reconcile loop over the declarative state f(desiredEnabled, hasConsent, online, serverIsUp, boundIp==nowIp); every trigger (user toggle, consent change, network callback, and a 10-second LAN-IP poll) only nudges a conflated Channel so no event is lost during in-flight actions, and all reconcile actions are idempotent.

The reconcile loop itself is the backoff: a reconcile exception sets state ERROR, records lastError, and doubles the wait from 5 seconds up to a 300-second cap, which is why GatewayServer.start() can stay non-blocking and non-throwing (bind failures surface via isRunning() rather than exceptions).

Reconcile state semantics: absent desired flag or consent leads to DISABLED — the runtime isEnabled flag is set false first, then the poller, heartbeat, EventUploader and SecureCommandPoller are stopped and the LAN server is stopped and dropped; offline leads to WAITING_FOR_NETWORK — deliberately never ERROR — where isEnabled is set false and the poller and heartbeat are stopped while EventUploader and SecureCommandPoller are not stopped but self-gate to zero HTTP on their own isEnabled + non-blank gmwebUrl gate, and the LAN server is intentionally left running; recovery from a degraded state (RECONNECTING/ERROR/WAITING_FOR_NETWORK) passes through RECONNECTING and reaches CONNECTED only after a fully successful rebind and idempotent starts of heartbeat, EventUploader, SecureCommandPoller, the poller (when gmwebUrl non-blank) and shadow sync, with isEnabled set true only at the very end; CONNECTING is declared and consumed by UI/notification mappings but never emitted by the current reconcile.

A stopped GatewayServer instance is not restartable by design — stop() closes the socket and shutdownNow()s both the acceptor and handler executors — so the supervisor always constructs a fresh GatewayServer via its factory whenever the server is not running or the bound address differs from the current LAN IPv4 (the DHCP-rebind case), and throws (loop → ERROR with backoff) if the fresh instance fails to bind.

retryNow (invoked on a validated-online network transition or the UI's manual reconnect) resets the loop backoff to 5s, revives a dead loop via the idempotent ensureLoop(), and calls HeartbeatManager.retryNow(), which resets the backoff ladder and wakes the pending backoff sleep through a conflated wake channel — so a brief WiFi re-association retries immediately instead of waiting out the 5-minute backoff ladder.

ConnectionSupervisor's public API: start() (idempotent, called from every ACTION_START entry — user toggle, boot receiver, START_STICKY revival) sets desiredEnabled and persists gatewayDesiredEnabled true then reconciles; stop() clears both and reconciles but deliberately does not stop the service (ACTION_STOP's own path does); shutdown() cancels the loop, stops the server and all five supervised components (heartbeat, outbox poller, EventUploader, SecureCommandPoller), sets DISABLED, and clears the process singleton.

NetworkMonitor is the single source of truth for 'validated internet': isOnline() requires both NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET and NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED (an up-but-unvalidated interface — captive portal, carrier drop — is not online), and onlineFlow() emits only on transitions via a registered NetworkCallback (callback-driven, distinctUntilChanged, zero polling), which the supervisor and the outbox poller use to wake immediately when the network flips back.

Boot recovery replays the user's persisted intent: BootGatewayReceiver, manifest-registered for BOOT_COMPLETED and LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED (though its guard currently acts only on BOOT_COMPLETED), proceeds only when gatewayDesiredEnabled and hasGatewayConsent are both true and then calls GatewayService.startGateway(context), which re-checks consent so a revoked consent is silently dropped.

The gateway state split: gatewayDesiredEnabled (gateway_desired_enabled) is the persisted user intent written only by supervisor start()/stop() and never touched by runtime teardown; isEnabled (gateway_enabled) is the runtime mirror true while components are up, written only by ConnectionSupervisor (false before stopping components on the disabled/offline paths, true only at the end of a fully successful reconcile) plus the consent-revocation reset; hasGatewayConsent is versioned (stored version >= CURRENT_CONSENT_VERSION, currently 1) so material data-use changes force a fresh opt-in, and revokeGatewayConsent() clears consent, desired, runtime, auto-start and cloud credentials.

GatewayAccessPolicy enforces consent at the boundaries: canStart(consent) gates the startGateway companion helper, the service's ACTION_START branch, and the watchdog scheduling, while canTransmit(consent, isEnabled) gates the HeartbeatManager loop, OutboxPoller loop, and WebhookEngine's local webhook dispatch; EventUploader (PR-02) and SecureCommandPoller (PR-10) do not consult canTransmit — each loop gates directly on prefs.isEnabled plus a non-blank gmwebUrl and idles with zero HTTP otherwise — so the durable outbox and the command transport still stop transmitting whenever the supervisor stops the gateway, even if the service process still lives.

GatewayServer runs a dedicated single-thread daemon acceptor so slow handlers can never starve accept(), a fixed 8-thread daemon handler pool, and a 10-second per-connection soTimeout bounding slowloris-style connections; start() is @Synchronized and non-throwing (bind failures are logged, isRunning() is the truth), and stop() also stops the EVE send queue whose lifecycle is tied to the server.

Since v2.6.10 GatewayServer parses HTTP in bytes, not characters: headers are read as raw bytes until CRLFCRLF (bare-LF blank line also terminates) capped at 32 KB, header count is capped at 100, the body is read as the exact Content-Length bytes with a 1 MB cap (413 over, 400 truncated), chunked Transfer-Encoding is rejected with 411, and the body is decoded as UTF-8 only after the full read — fixing the mis-parsing/stalling of multi-byte UTF-8 bodies (Persian text, emoji) caused by the old char-based Content-Length treatment.

GatewayServer authenticates with constant-time comparison: the key from X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer is compared via MessageDigest.isEqual (timing-side-channel resistant); GET /health is deliberately reachable without authentication per the EVE spec while /ready and all other endpoints require a valid key, and the API key is auto-generated on first use as 'gw_' plus 128 CSPRNG bits.

GatewayServer applies per-client-IP brute-force lockout: 8 failed auth attempts within a 10-minute window trigger a 5-minute lockout during which requests receive 429 without a key comparison; a successful auth clears the per-IP failure record, and the failure map is purged of stale entries above 64 records so it cannot grow unbounded.

The gateway's default port is 8080 (GatewayPreferences.DEFAULT_PORT), and unless bindAllInterfaces is set the server binds only to the first detected non-loopback LAN IPv4 address (getLocalIpAddress(), with reuseAddress enabled) to limit exposure to the local network; bindAllInterfaces=true binds 0.0.0.0, which also disables the supervisor's stale-IP rebind check since 0.0.0.0 matches any address.

Since v2.6.10 GatewayServer hardens the MMS image surface: remote REST callers may only supply https:// imageUrl values whose host resolves to a public address (loopback, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, 0.0.0.0/8, and IPv6 link/site-local/ULA ranges are refused; content:// is no longer accepted from remote callers), and downloads are capped at 10 MB with redirects disabled and 10s/15s connect/read timeouts.

Gateway secrets (API key, webhook signing secret, cloud bearer token, registration secret) are encrypted at rest with SecureStore — AES/GCM/NoPadding under a 256-bit hardware-backed Android Keystore key, payload Base64(iv || ciphertext) under the 'enc:v1:' prefix — with legacy plaintext values transparently re-encrypted on first read; since v2.6.10 persistence is fail-closed: if the Keystore is unavailable the secret is not persisted at all (storeEncrypted throws) rather than degrading to plaintext.

All outbound gateway URLs are HTTPS-only by construction: the backendUrl and gmwebUrl preference setters require an https:// scheme (empty = GMweb bridge disabled), the default backend URL comes from the build-time GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL BuildConfig field, and WebhookEngine rejects non-https webhook URLs at dispatch time — so the cloud bearer token and webhook payloads never cross plaintext HTTP.

Beyond /health and /ready, GatewayServer routes the EVE provider contract (POST /send, GET /send/status/{id}, POST /send/cancel/{id}, GET /send/capacity, backed by the persisted EveSmsQueue), scheduled-send CRUD under /api/v1/sms/schedule via GatewayScheduler, and the app API (/api/v1/sms/send with explicit 202-accepted/503-rejected outcomes instead of lying 200s, /api/v1/sms with filters, /api/v1/sms/inbox, /api/v1/mms/send, /api/v1/status), and error responses deliberately avoid leaking internal exception details to API clients.

The gateway subsystem has five focused pure-JVM unit tests (no @RunWith/Robolectric): GatewayAccessPolicyTest (full truth tables of canStart/canTransmit), EveSmsQueueTest over EveSmsQueue.MemoryStore (priority ordering, idempotency keys, queued-to-active-to-sent/failed status flow, cancellation rules, per-priority capacity, GMweb-compatible verification fields), GatewayEventFactoryTest (deterministic message/event UUIDs, envelope.v1 round-trip at cryptoVersion 0, rejection of unknown crypto versions), GatewaySyncPolicyTest (LOCK 13 batch caps of 100 events / 512 KiB, lone-oversized-event rule, full-jitter backoff bounds capped at 5 min), and GatewaySyncSchemaTest (pins the additive MIGRATION_6_7 CREATE TABLE/INDEX statements against KSP-generated 7.json, including the exactly-once UNIQUE indexes); ConnectionSupervisor, GatewayServer and EventUploader themselves are Android-dependent and have no direct JVM unit tests, and the androidTest source set additionally contains the stock ExampleInstrumentedTest.

Since PR-02 the gateway's cloud-event path is durable rather than fire-and-forget: events are committed to the Room table gateway_event_outbox inside the same Room transaction that lands the message, and the EventUploader (wired into GatewayService.onCreate and owned by the supervisor through ManagedComponents startEventUploader/stopEventUploader) is the only transmitter — its loop first re-queues SENDING rows left behind by a crash (recoverSending), then claims batches transactionally and POSTs to /api/v1/agent/events/batch, applying partial ACKs (accepted[] → ACKED with serverSequence; the rest → PENDING with attempt-counted backoff), full-batch requeue on transport failure, and DEAD_LETTER on permanent 4xx rejects (429 excluded) or undecodable payloads, so nothing is silently dropped; the loop idles with zero HTTP while prefs.isEnabled is false or gmwebUrl is blank.

Gateway event identity is deterministic (TechSpec §13): messageId is nameUUIDFromBytes of 'source:providerId:createdAtMs' and eventUuid of 'evt:<eventType>:source:providerId:dateMs', so the UNIQUE(eventUuid) index makes rebuilds of the same event a no-op dedupe via insertOrIgnore (exactly-once); payload bytes are stored as a crypto-ready envelope (encoding envelope.v1, cryptoVersion 0 = UTF-8 JSON today, AEAD ciphertext with cryptoVersion ≥ 1 in Phase 7 with zero schema change, unknown versions rejected by decodePayloadEnvelope); the backing v6→v7 Room migration (UPGRADE_TO_V7_SQL / MIGRATION_6_7) is purely additive — 5 tables plus 7 indexes including index_gateway_event_outbox_eventUuid, index_remote_commands_idempotencyKey and index_remote_conversation_map_threadId.

PR-02 deleted WebhookEngine's fire-and-forget cloud dispatch path — cloud events are now committed to gateway_event_outbox and transmitted by EventUploader with retry/ACK; the object survives solely for the user-configured LOCAL webhook on incoming SMS: best-effort by design, consent-gated (GatewayAccessPolicy.canTransmit) and HTTPS-only, POSTing an sms_received JSON payload signed with HMAC-SHA256 over '<timestamp>.<body>' in the X-Signature header when a webhook secret is configured.

PR-10's SecureCommandPoller is the fifth supervised component and the strategic command transport: an outbound-only HTTPS long-poll of POST /api/v1/agent/commands/claim (agentId 'android-agent', limit 25, per-device ES256 signature via AgentAuth with X-API-Key as legacy fallback, 2 s quiet cadence on empty claims, 5 s retry after a failed cycle). Claimed rows are ingested exactly-once into the durable remote_commands queue via INSERT OR IGNORE on the unique idempotencyKey index; redeliveries are never double-executed — the poller only re-reports the durable local state through POST /api/v1/agent/commands/{id}/status (guarded lifecycle ACCEPTED→EXECUTING→COMPLETED/FAILED); SEND_SMS rows execute immediately through the GatewayOutgoingPipeline funnel while the legacy OutboxPoller remains the compatibility transport. The loop self-gates on prefs.isEnabled plus a non-blank gmwebUrl (zero HTTP until CONNECTED).

androidTest additionally hosts the device-only GatewayDurabilityDeviceTest (PR-01..04 process-death contract, run via ./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest) alongside the stock ExampleInstrumentedTest: it enrolls the real Keystore device identity (three 65-byte public points), proves command redelivery is deduped by the unique idempotencyKey index, verifies guarded markCommandState transitions reject illegal state jumps (e.g. RECEIVED→COMPLETED), and checks recoverSending() requeues crash-window SENDING outbox rows.
